explain: The guide confirms 65 total questions including unscored pretest items, but the exact unscored count is undisclosed and items are indistinguishable, so candidates cannot reverse-engineer the scored denominator.

q: Two answers both improve accuracy, but the stem says MOST cost-effective. Which should the candidate choose?
options: The option meeting requirements at the lowest cost, even if marginally less accurate
The most expensive option, since higher price always means a better exam answer
The option with the most services combined, regardless of its cost or need
The option requiring custom hardware, since complexity signals higher quality
explain: Cost-qualifier stems rank acceptable solutions by cost: among options meeting requirements, the cheapest adequate one is the key, not the priciest or most complex.
source: Adattata da Udemy – practice test MLA-C01

q: A multiple-response item asks for TWO services that together monitor drift and bias. A candidate selects only one correct service. How is it scored?
options: It earns half credit automatically for the one correct selection alone
It is marked incorrect, since all required choices must be selected together
It is entirely excluded from scoring as an unusual experimental response pattern
It earns bonus credit for answering faster with fewer selected choices
explain: Multiple-response items require the complete correct set with no partial credit. Selecting only one of two required choices makes the whole item incorrect.

q: A candidate needs extra time or accommodations for a disability. What is the proper path?
options: Ask the proctor on exam day to improvise extra time for them on the spot
Bring a personal assistant into the testing room without any prior approval
Request accommodations in advance through the official Pearson VUE process
Pause the exam timer manually whenever a personal break is needed
explain: Accommodations must be requested and approved ahead of the appointment via the official accommodations process. They cannot be granted ad hoc by the proctor or self-administered.

q: During an online-proctored MLA-C01 session, which candidate behavior is most likely to trigger a policy violation?
options: Sitting alone in a quiet private room with a clear desk and ID ready
Keeping eyes on the screen while following all proctor instructions closely
Testing the microphone and camera during the initial system check routine
Reaching for a mobile phone or having another person enter the room
explain: Online proctoring forbids phones, notes, and other people in the testing space, with room scans and webcam monitoring. Using a phone or admitting someone is a classic violation.
source: Adattata da Udemy – practice test MLA-C01

q: A candidate masters Domain 3 (22%) but neglects Domain 1 (28%) and still passes. What does this prove about MLA-C01 scoring?
options: That domain weights shape preparation priority, but only the 720 total decides the outcome
That Domain 3 alone guarantees a pass regardless of every other domain result
That Domain 1 questions are all unscored items and can be safely ignored
That each domain requires its own separate 720 score to pass the overall exam
explain: Weights indicate content share and study priority, yet the pass/fail line is the single compensatory 720 total. Strength in a small domain can combine with enough points elsewhere to pass despite a weak large domain.
